---
title: "Hands-on Exercise 2"
subtitle: "Thematic Mapping and GeoVisualisation with R"
---

This exercise develops clear thematic maps from geospatial data and explores how classification, symbols, layout, and interactivity affect what a map communicates.

::: {.chapter-link}
[Open the course reference for Chapter 2](https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap02.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::

## Learning focus

- Import and prepare the required spatial and attribute data.
- Build choropleth maps with `tmap`.
- Compare variables through small-multiple maps.
- Highlight spatial features that meet a selection criterion.
- Combine thematic maps with statistical charts.
- Create an interactive map for exploration.

## Analysis workflow

1. Check the spatial data, attributes, and coordinate reference system.
2. Select a meaningful variable and appropriate classification method.
3. Design a readable static thematic map with suitable labels and legend.
4. Compare patterns with small multiples or a supporting chart.
5. Add interactivity where it improves exploration of the data.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Map design choices should be justified by the analytical question, not only by visual appearance.
:::
